production.direction_en: Night in the cathedral refuge. Mahmut sits apart with his breastplate across his knees, turning it so the empty crest socket catches candlelight. Aveline brings him bread he does not eat.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: You have been polishing a hole for an hour.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: It was a crown once. I took it off with a smith's hammer.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: Why a hammer?

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: A knife would have been neater. I did not want it to be neat.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: And the woman in the tower. You told Fadyme you did not know her.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: If I tell her what I saw that night, she will stop sleeping. One of us should sleep.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: A shield that hides the sky is still a roof. People can suffocate under roofs.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Then I will lift it. Not tonight.

production.direction_en: After Cael's reflection fades. The others sleep on the outer dais. Marek keeps watch; Mahmut cannot sit still.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: You have walked this dais forty times. The stones have no new answers.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: He asked for an hour that belongs to me. Which one?

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: I read your treason on the western road. Every village asked what hour you ran. I never knew.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: The hour I stopped obeying. That was the only one I ever chose.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: Then perhaps that is the one he wants.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Then he wants the only thing I would not give back.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: Behind them, Fadyme turned in her sleep. Neither man said the rest aloud.

production.direction_en: A curtained cot in the Undercity ward. Fadyme opens her mother's prayer book; the folded letter from the forest road sits between two psalms. Clem pretends to sort chalk.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: You refold that letter every time you think no one is looking.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You are looking.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: I am a professional. Graves, registers, letters. Who is it for?

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: For after. He is not allowed to read it before.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: After is a long word to put on paper.

commands.speaker: fadyme_thought
commands.text: Mother wrote her prayers in the margins. I write my apologies. We were always untidy in the same places.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Clem. If I forget where I put it, remind me. If I forget you, forgive me.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: I remember names for a living. Yours is in good hands.

production.direction_en: Between the Ashen estate and the altar, the company splits onto safe roads. For two days it is only Mahmut and Fadyme, a stolen goat-cheese, and a stream too cold to wash in.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You cut the cheese like it owes the Crown money.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: It does. I paid for it.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You traded a buckle you did not need for cheese we did not need. That is the best purchase you have made in six years.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: You are laughing.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: I am allowed. Write it down somewhere. Today I was not a seal or an heir. I was a woman with cheese.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: I will remember it.

commands.speaker: fadyme_thought
commands.text: He means it. That is why I did not say: remember it for me.

production.direction_en: Kera rebuilds her cart in the Oakhaven square, relabeling every bottle in red ink. Nixie hands her the wrong one on purpose.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: That is not a tonic. That is a very small explosion with a cork.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: The label says tonic.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: Labels lie. People write them. I label everything twice now.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: Twice?

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: Once for what it is. Once for who might want it for the wrong reason.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: That second label must be very long.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: Since the orchard, it just says: the Guild.

production.direction_en: The antidote archive after the Matron's fall. Kera finds a ledger in her own apprentice handwriting.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: This is mine. My hand. Blood analyses, three winters ago.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: You were an apprentice. Apprentices analyze what they are handed.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: The client column is blank on every page. I never asked. I was proud they trusted me with the difficult samples.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Were any of them hers?

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: The last sample says "heir line, maternal". I wrote "stable, remarkable" beside it.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Then write something truer beside it now. You are still holding the pen.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: "Incomplete." That is the only honest word I have.

production.direction_en: Kera returns to the Undercity market to post a notice: the ledger wing's patrons, named in her careful script. A merchant tears it down; she pins it up again.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: You can tear it down forty times. I have forty copies and very good paste.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: He was one of your Guild's oldest patrons.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: He paid for glass that drank people. He can pay for the paste.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: When they come for you, and they will, where will you be?

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: In the archive. With the door open. That is the point.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: Then I will leave a lantern at your door.

production.direction_en: Dawn after the reveal. Kera writes by lantern at the edge of the dais while Fadyme sleeps.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: He said he can return her hours. A man who keeps an hour in his pocket is a man who has a mechanism.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Can you build one?

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: Not yet. "Yet" is doing a great deal of work in that sentence.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Then what do you need?

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: The glass bell's ward, a clean sample, time. The one thing she does not have.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Then we steal time from somewhere else.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: Careful. That is exactly what he would say.

production.direction_en: Brin leads a line of forest refugees through the ash trees. A child counts bells on her fingers.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: Stay on the road. The trees whisper; they do not bite.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: A bell rang somewhere west. Every refugee stopped walking.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: Keep walking. If you stop for every bell, the road wins.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: Say your name when you pass the shrine. Loud. The bell likes to know who is still here.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: One by one they said their names. Brin said hers last, quietly, as if it cost more.

production.direction_en: Brin visits the alder behind the wayshrine where her father carved his name. Two letters are already gone. The old keeper follows her out.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: B-R-. It used to be longer.

commands.speaker: shrine_keeper
commands.text: I can recut it. I keep a chisel for the register board.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: If you cut it, it will just be your letters.

commands.speaker: shrine_keeper
commands.text: Then say his name while I cut. Then the letters are yours.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: Bram Alder. He could split a log with one swing and could not split a word to save his life.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: The chisel bit. The name held.

production.direction_en: Rain on the lowland refuge. Nixie has come over from Oakhaven with the woodcutters. Two shelters are sagging; Brin can brace only one.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: If I hold the east roof, the west falls. If I hold the west—

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: You said that at the shrine. Word for word. I was there.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: And he said I did not have to hold it alone.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: Everyone who can lift, to the west roof. Children to the east. Now!

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: Twelve pairs of hands took the west beam. Brin held the east alone, and for once it was the smaller weight.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: Twelve hands and one stubborn woodcutter. That is a road.

production.direction_en: The lower pass below the altar. Brin's refugees are through; she tightens her straps.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: You will take them the rest of the way. I am going up.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: Up is where the eclipse is. Up is terrifying.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: I told a knight to keep up. It would be rude to be late.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: Then I am coming too. Someone has to build the barricade.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: You are going to set it on fire.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: Only a little!

production.direction_en: Nixie spreads the false map on a stump and traces the road the wolves learned.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: Someone drew this road on purpose. Look, the ink goes around the shrine, not through it.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: To lead travelers away from the shrine?

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: To lead them away from the names. The shrine keeps the register. No register, no one knows you passed.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Then whoever drew it wanted people to disappear quietly.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: Or wanted one person to. I am keeping this map. I collect liars.

production.direction_en: The Oakhaven road register survived the blank-board night. Nixie finds a page from eighteen winters ago.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: "Girl, about one year. No family. Vale." That is all I was for a while.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: It is a lovely hand, though. Whoever wrote it took care.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: They wrote the same care for two hundred Vales. It is a road word. It means nobody.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: It means somebody found you on a road and wrote you down so the bell would know you. That is not nobody.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: You are going to make a song of this. Are you not?

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: Only a short one.

production.direction_en: At the refuge, children with register marks crowd around Nixie's bow.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: You are all Vales? Every one of you?

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: Seven small hands went up. Then an eighth, belonging to an old man who laughed at himself.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: Then listen. The name means the road found you. So you get to choose where the road goes next.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: That is a better sermon than the cathedral gave.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: The cathedral never got chased up a tree.

production.direction_en: Before the stair, Nixie pins a new mark on her map: not a town, just a circle around where the company camps.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: I never marked a place as home. It felt like lying to the map.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: That circle is around us.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: Yes. It moves. It is a very inconvenient home.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: It is the only one I would follow.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: Good. Then nobody is staying behind.

production.direction_en: The pilgrim refuge after the Choir Knights fall. Aveline lights candles one by one, counting heads.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: Forty-one candles. Forty-one pilgrims. The last one is lit.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You counted twice.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: I always count twice. Once for the living, once for anyone the bell might have missed.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: And if the count is short?

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: Then I do not leave the door. That is the whole of my theology.

production.direction_en: In the sacristy, an old priest asks Aveline to hear his confession.

commands.speaker: old_priest
commands.text: Sister. We kept the heirs' names in the book of offerings. Seven in my lifetime.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: In the book of offerings. Not the book of the dead?

commands.speaker: old_priest
commands.text: The dead are mourned. Offerings are thanked. It was easier to thank them.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: And the princess who came through this nave today?

commands.speaker: old_priest
commands.text: Her line is in the book, Sister. With no date. We were waiting.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: Then I will take the book. And I will not thank anyone.

production.direction_en: After the name is written back. Aveline rewrites the offering prayer in the margin of the old book.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: "We give thanks for those who were offered." No.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: You are editing scripture.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: I am correcting a record. You taught me that.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: "We remember those who were taken, and we name them, so the living stand witness."

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: That one I would copy.

production.direction_en: Night after the reveal. Aveline sits at Fadyme's side while Mahmut walks the dais.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You are keeping vigil. I am not dead, Sister.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: A vigil is for the living. The dead do not need company.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Your church thanked seven women like me.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: My church will learn to say their names. I will stand at your door until you tell me to go.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: And if I never do?

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: Then it will be a very long vigil. I brought extra candles.

production.direction_en: Sable and Rikka wait out a patrol inside the signal tower. Sable turns an old courier token in her fingers.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: You go quiet when you see wax. Real quiet. Quieter than usual, which is impressive.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: I carried sealed orders when I was fifteen. Seven notches paid double.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: Did you ever open one?

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: Couriers who open orders become messages themselves.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: That is the most horrifying thing anyone has said to me, and I have been on fire.

production.direction_en: After Oren leaves the span, Sable searches his abandoned command post and finds the first Council commission he ever received to hunt the heir, six years old.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: This courier knot is mine. I tied it. I carried this to him.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: You could not have known what it said.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: I knew it paid double. That was enough for me to not ask.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: I carried orders for years for less than double.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: Then we are both deliveries. I am going to the estate alone. I have one more thing to carry.

production.direction_en: The night before the company arrives. Sable slips into the estate's servant wing and finds a dozen people locked in the dark.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: Do not speak. Nod. How long have you been here?

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: A cook raised ten fingers. Then ten again.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: Twenty days. And the master?

commands.speaker: estate_servant
commands.text: The master has been dead for years, miss. The house still gives orders.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: Then the house can wait for a knight. I will open the door from inside.

production.direction_en: Sable leaves the last lantern at the final turn and tells Hana the one thing she has never said.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: Why lanterns? You could just remember the way.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: When I was a courier, I was told the dark was safer. It is. For the person carrying the secret.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: I carried the order that sent Oren after her. I have told no one else.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: You told me.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: You kept Fadyme's secret. I thought you would know what to do with mine.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: Light it. That is what I would do.

production.direction_en: The ward's first night. Three patients become nine.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Nine patients, one table. Iona, triage. Anyone with a joke, out.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: I was not joking. I was complaining.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: You. Bleeding one. Why did you not say?

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: It is a small cut.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: It is a small cut on a very pale woman. Sit. I have seen that pallor on the salt road.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Please do not write it down.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: I write everything down. I will also forget where I put it. That is my best offer.

production.direction_en: The ward is quiet. Tilda cleans sea-glass vials and talks about her teacher.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: My teacher treated salt-fever on the coast road. She never promised anyone anything.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: You say that as if it were cruel.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: It was the kindest thing she did. The dying planned. The living did not wait for miracles.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: And the elixir Fadyme carries?

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Is a promise in a bottle. I hate it.

production.direction_en: The field infirmary. A servant asks Tilda how long her husband has.

commands.speaker: estate_servant
commands.text: How long, healer? Please. The truth.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Days. Perhaps a week. He will be comfortable.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You told her.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Now she will spend those days talking to him instead of guarding his door.

commands.speaker: fadyme_thought
commands.text: And I spent mine guarding a door.

production.direction_en: After the battle, Tilda wedges the infirmary door open with a brick.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Doors in clinics stay open. Rule one.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Tilda. How long does she have?

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Ask her. Then sit down, because she will tell you.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: She already did.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Then you know more than any healer here. Go and spend it.

production.direction_en: Waiting for dark in the tower, Rikka tells Sable about home.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: In the kiln towns we ring tassels in the streets when the bells ring. Confuses the counting!

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: Does it work?

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: No. But people stop crying to yell at us. That works.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: So you are loud on purpose.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: Quiet means the bell is winning. I refuse.

production.direction_en: Rikka returns to her kiln company after the bridge and leads a procession for names lost on the road.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: Tassels up! Every name you shout gets a spark!

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: The street filled with names and sparks. An old potter shouted one twice, then stopped, unable to say it a third time.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: Hey. I will say it with you. What was it?

commands.speaker: old_potter
commands.text: Mira. My granddaughter.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: MIRA! There. Now the whole street has it.

production.direction_en: After the outer stair holds, Rikka inspects her still-smoking barricade.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: It is on fire.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: It is warm. There is a difference.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: It stopped two sentinels for forty seconds.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: Did you hear that? Forty seconds. That is a professional number.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: You were scared.

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: ...Terrified. Do not tell anyone. It ruins my brand.

production.direction_en: The night after the reveal. Rikka sits beside the sleeping Fadyme and, for once, says nothing.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: Rikka did not ring her tassel. She held it still in her fist so it would not wake anyone.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You are being quiet. Am I dying faster?

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: No! I just thought you might like to hear something that was not a bell.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: What is it?

commands.speaker: rikka_ember
commands.text: Everyone breathing. Listen. None of them are counting.

production.direction_en: Mirel studies the scraped register with a reading lens while the others rest.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: Look at the margin. Someone practiced the heir's initial three times before cutting the line.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Practiced?

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: Scribes test a pen before a difficult name. Whoever erased this was trained at court.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You know the style.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: I know every court style. It is an unpleasant talent.

production.direction_en: After the gallery, Mirel sits alone with the erasure order she recognized.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: I copied forty of these the month after Crownfall. Forty names removed. I timed myself.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: You did not know whose names they were.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: I knew they were names. That should have been enough.

commands.speaker: sister_aveline
commands.text: Then what will you do with the hand that copied them?

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: Make it write them back. One by one. It will take longer than removing them did.

production.direction_en: On the road to the altar, Mirel writes a formal correction of the erasure orders she copied and signs it with her court seal.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: The moment I seal this, the Council will know a court scribe recanted.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: They branded me for less.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: That is not as comforting as you think.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: It was not meant to comfort. It was meant to say you will have company.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: The wax took the seal cleanly. Mirel's hand did not shake until afterward.

production.direction_en: Dawn. Mirel reads a list aloud at the edge of the dais: every erased name she has found in court, cathedral and Guild ledgers, now written back.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: Corwen Hale. Liss Aubry. Tomas Pike.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: Stop. Read that one again.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: Tomas Pike. Undercity register. Removed by order, two winters ago.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: My brother.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: He was not one of mine. He is on my list now. He is witnessed.

production.direction_en: Odelia marks the cistern walls with chalk arrows. One old arrow is already there, faded.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: This one is not mine. The knot at the tail is a harbor knot.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Someone from the coast came down here.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: My brother drew arrows like this. He came down two winters ago.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: And you followed.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: I dislike unanswered tracks. This one is the loudest.

production.direction_en: In the Guild archive, Kera finds a ledger line with a harbor knot drawn beside it.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: "Pike, T. Coastal. Sample complete." There is a knot doodled next to it.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: He always drew it when he was bored. He was bored because they made him wait.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: Odelia, the entry says complete. It does not say released.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: Then the track ends here.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: The ledger ends here. Tracks are your department.

production.direction_en: Before the bell pulse, Odelia checks the third span alone.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: Hollow stones. Same chalk arrow at the base. He came this way before the Guild took him.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You keep walking where he walked.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: If I walk it all, maybe I will understand why he stopped.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Or you will understand why you kept going.

production.direction_en: After Mirel reads his name. Odelia draws one last chalk arrow on the altar stone, pointing out.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: Every arrow he drew pointed down. Into the dark. Toward whatever he was chasing.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: This one points out.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: It is for him. So he knows the way back up.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Then the track is answered.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: Yes. I can stop now. I do not think I will.

production.direction_en: The inn after the registry was saved. Pippa writes lyrics on a napkin.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: Forty-two names rhyme with nothing. I am going to make them rhyme with each other.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: You could just read them out.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: A list is forgotten by supper. A song gets stuck in your head for a week. Which one do you want your name in?

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: ...The song.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: Everybody picks the song.

production.direction_en: At the refuge, Pippa's bell charm trembles against her wrist though no bell is ringing.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: I bought it from a refugee from the capital. She said it came off a bell that stopped.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: A bell that stopped?

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: She said the whole city went quiet one night. The charm has shivered ever since.

commands.speaker: fadyme_thought
commands.text: The silenced bell. Mother said it was the first to fail.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Keep it close. Somebody may want it back one day.

production.direction_en: After the record accepts Fadyme's name, the charm at Pippa's wrist rings on its own, once.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: It rang. It has never rung. It only shivers.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: It rang when the name was written.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: Like it was answering.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Or like it recognized someone.

production.direction_en: Midday, leaving the crater. Pippa sings the Oakhaven names for the road down, then adds one more verse.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: Last verse. New name. Fadyme Veyr, who came through Oakhaven and did not let it forget her.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You made it rhyme.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: Veyr rhymes with stayed here. Almost. Close enough for a road song.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Sing it again. Louder than the paper.

production.direction_en: The civilians are across. Nara measures the gate chains with a knotted cord.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: Eleven knots. My mother's gate held for fourteen. I am three short.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You measure yourself against a gate?

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: Vell wardens measure everything. Seconds, spans, people. It keeps fear busy.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: What is my measure?

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: You walk slower on the left. You hide it well. Not well enough for a Vell.

production.direction_en: Nara watches the empty far end of the span where Oren stood.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: My mother trained him on this bridge. First rule: the gate is for the people behind it, not the order in front of it.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: He forgot.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: He remembered today. Late. The gate is still open because of it.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: You saw him leave.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: I saw him stay until the last cart crossed. What he did after is his to answer for, not mine to guess.

production.direction_en: Escorting survivors toward the lower pass, Nara stops at a broken cart in a ditch.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: It is old. Before our time on this road.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: No. Three winters. I counted the wheels. I could not reach it before the span dropped.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: And you still count.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: If I stop counting, I stop being a warden. I become a woman standing near a ditch.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: You can be both for one minute. I will watch the road.

production.direction_en: Dawn after the reveal. Nara finds Mahmut staring at the estate road on a map.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: You are looking for Oren.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: He knew enough to send men after her. He may know what the Court is.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: He was alive when he left the span. That is all I know. I will not pretend to more.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: That is not help.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: It is the truth. You have had enough of the other kind.

production.direction_en: Before the private reading, Clem makes a rubbing of an old grave slab in the archive room.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Every grave down here has a name under the moss. Most people just never bring charcoal.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You enjoy this.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Enormously. The dead are very patient about being remembered. The living are terrible at it.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Then do me a kindness today. Forget what you hear in that room.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: That is the one thing I am bad at.

production.direction_en: After the elixir lie. Clem corners Fadyme between patient cots.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: He asked me what the alchemist said. I told him to ask you. That was the smallest lie I could manage.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Thank you.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Do not thank me. I record names so people are not forgotten. You are asking me to help him not know you.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: I am asking you to let me choose when.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Then choose before I have to carve it.

production.direction_en: Behind the servants' wing, a row of graves with no names at all.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Nineteen graves. Not a letter. Not even a date.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: Maybe they could not write.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Somebody could dig. Somebody could have written "here". Nobody did.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: I will come back with charcoal. Everyone gets at least a "here".

production.direction_en: After the confession, Clem sits beside Mahmut, holding a stick of charcoal she does not use.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: I knew. Since the Undercity. I am sorry.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: She asked you to keep it.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: She asked. I agreed. I am still sorry. Both are true.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Then keep one more thing for me. Her name, every day, in your book. In case the world starts to forget it.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Every day. In my best hand.

production.direction_en: In the conservatory, Vespera tells Iona about the first time she saw the ward.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: The Guild's lowest cistern. The water did not reflect the lantern. It reflected the hour before.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: And you went closer.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: Of course. I am a scholar. It is our only vice, and it is enough.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: What did it cost?

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: Ask me in the next scene. I would like one more scene before I answer.

production.direction_en: Later that night, beneath the stone arch.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: To read the ward, I let it read me. It took hours. I do not know how many.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You traded your own time.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: Knowingly. That is the difference between me and you. I chose my price.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Do you regret it?

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: I regret nothing I learned. I regret how tired the mornings are.

production.direction_en: The conservatory after the Wraith falls. The glass panes still show a room long gone.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: It is a nursery. Look. A cradle, a bell pin on the pillow.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: That was mine.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: Then the glass has been keeping your absence for fifteen years. That is loyalty, of a kind.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Can you make it stop?

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: I can. Should I?

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: ...Not yet.

production.direction_en: Dawn after Cael's offer. Vespera gives Mahmut her verdict.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: Hours can move between people. With a witness and consent. He is not lying about that.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Then he can do it.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: He can do something. He did not tell you what the hour carries with it. Hours are not empty rooms.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: What does that mean?

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: It means we find out before you consent, not after. I have paid for learning too late.

production.direction_en: After the rescue, Hana sits on the step, staring at her hands.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: They were shaking. The whole time. I thought everyone could see.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: Everyone could.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: Oh.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: And every child is outside. So the shaking did not matter. Only the door did.

production.direction_en: After the collapse, Hana washes dust off her face and does not look at Fadyme's sleeve.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You are not looking at my arm very carefully.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: I promised. Not looking is part of it.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: It is a heavy promise. I am sorry I gave it to you.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: I carry traps up mountains. I can carry this. But it is heavier than a trap.

production.direction_en: Hana leads the evacuees along Sable's lanterns, counting them as they pass.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: Thirty-two. Thirty-three. That is everyone.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: You did not stammer once.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: I was counting. It is hard to be afraid and count at the same time.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: Nara says the same thing. You two should start a very quiet club.

production.direction_en: After the confession, Hana finds Fadyme awake.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: He knows now. So I can stop keeping it.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You can.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: Then I want to say it once, out loud, so it is not stuck in me. You were very brave, and it was very unfair.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Both are true.

commands.speaker: hana_birch
commands.text: Both are true.

production.direction_en: While Fadyme is inside the archive room, Thistle waits outside and shows Mahmut a pressed flower.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: At the m-monastery we plant in bell-ash. Most things die. This one does not.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: What is it?

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: We call it owing-bell. It only blooms where an hour is owed. Graves, mostly. Sometimes the sick.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: Why show me?

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: Because I d-do not know how to say the other thing. So I am showing you a flower.

production.direction_en: In the field infirmary, a pot of owing-bell opens as Fadyme walks past.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: It opened.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Please do not tell him what it means.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: I will not. But I will not lie about flowers. If he asks, I will say it is blooming.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: That is fair.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: I am sorry. It is a beautiful flower. It is a terrible flower.

production.direction_en: A ward cracks under the pulse. Thistle rebuilds it with thorn-cord and prayer.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: Hold still. Wards are like fences. You mend them from the inside.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: You are not stammering.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: I never stammer when my hands know what they are doing.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: Then keep your hands busy all night.

production.direction_en: The lower pass, the first evening of the road down. Thistle presses a small packet into Fadyme's hand.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: Winter seeds. You plant them before the frost, not after.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: I may not see spring, Thistle.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: That is not what they are for. They are for planting. Somebody else sees the spring. That is how gardens work.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Then I will plant them somewhere he walks every day.

production.direction_en: Iona hangs her river lantern above the ward door.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: On the river we hang lanterns so the lost can find the shore. Living or not.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Do the dead come?

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: Their names do. We read them aloud as the boats pass. That is how they are witnessed.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Would you read mine, if it came to that?

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: I would rather read it while you are here to correct my pronunciation.

production.direction_en: After the Matron. Iona floats paper boats down the cistern, one for each name in the Guild's ledger.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: One hundred and six names. I will read them all.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: That will take all night.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: It took them longer to be forgotten.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: ...Give me half. I have a loud voice.

production.direction_en: The ward holds. Iona listens to the wounded rather than examining them.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: Tell me your name. Then tell me who is waiting for you.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: A young sentry could not remember. Iona waited. After a long time, a name came: his sister's.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: Good. Hold on to her. That is your lantern tonight.

production.direction_en: The first night on the road down. Iona lights her river lantern at the edge of camp and makes an offer to Fadyme.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: If the curse takes names, then someone should say yours every night. Out loud. Where the bells can hear.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Every night is a long promise.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: River keepers do it for strangers. You are not a stranger.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Then I accept. Pronounce it well.

production.direction_en: Jori rebuilds the forge gate hinge while the village sleeps.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: This hinge was my grandmother's pattern. Everything here is. She made bridges, gates, chains.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: You make shields.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: Because gates get broken and chains get used. A shield goes where the person goes.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: That is a good reason to walk with us.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: It is the only reason. Do not make it sentimental.

production.direction_en: Home after the Undercity. Jori finds her grandmother's chain die in the forge cellar, stamped with a seven-notched mark.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: Seven notches. On our die. On OUR die.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: She may not have known what it meant.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: Smiths always know what their iron is for. We just stop asking.

commands.speaker: brin_alder
commands.text: You are asking now.

production.direction_en: Jori climbs the Oakhaven bell frame. The Harvest Bell was cast in her family's forge.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: We cast it for festivals. It counts hours. We never knew.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: She laid her palm on the bronze. It was warm, though the morning was cold.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: If a bell can be made, it can be unmade. I just have to find the right tool.

production.direction_en: Dawn. Jori studies the broken chain links scattered across the dais.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: We broke the chains. The bells kept ringing. Breaking is not enough.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: What is?

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: A key. Something that opens the lock instead of smashing the door. My family made the lock. I will make the key.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: How long?

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: Longer than I want. Shorter than she needs, if I stop talking. Go away.

production.direction_en: The refugees are across. Marek admits why he recognized the crest.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: I read your treason aloud in eleven villages. "The knight Mahmut, oath-breaker, abandoned the heir."

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: You believed it.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: I believed it was paper. Paper is what heralds carry. I stopped carrying paper after that.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: And now?

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: Now I carry people. They are heavier and more honest.

production.direction_en: Marek keeps a column of refugees walking by singing a counting song.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: One for the road and two for the rain, three for the ones who will walk it again.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: Your rhythm is off by a half-step on the uphill.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: On purpose. The old ones need the half-step.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: ...That is good wardening.

production.direction_en: In a village square on the estate road, Marek unrolls a blank herald's scroll and speaks from memory.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: Hear me. Six years ago I read you a decree. It was false. The knight Mahmut did not abandon the heir. He defied the order to give her up.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: The square was silent. Then an old woman said, "Then who gave the order?"

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: That, grandmother, is the right question. Ask it loudly.

production.direction_en: Leaving the crater. Marek walks at the head of the column, playing softly, without a pennant on his spear.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: You never fly a banner.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: A banner tells people where to march. I would rather they decided.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: Then where will you march next?

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: Wherever he goes looking for that Court. Someone has to keep the rhythm.
Every life holds counted hours. They can be taken, given, or owed, but never moved without a witness and consent.
House Veyr bound seven bells to count the hours of the living. They do not heal. They keep the ledger.
An hour cannot be written without a name that remembers it. That is why Veyrhold carves names on trees and doors.
Bodies left behind by unpaid hours. Their names are gone; their hours are not.
Six years ago the capital fell, the king died, and the chancellor was recorded dead. The Council of Dukes has ruled since.
Children with no registered family are written into road registers as "Vale". It is a common name, and a lonely one.
The mark of the Royal Inquisition, keepers of sealed records. Its seals still appear on orders no one admits writing.
Alchemists and physicians. One wing keeps antidotes; the other kept a ledger of people.
He taught that a bell is a prayer the whole village hears, and that names spoken aloud are witnesses for the living.
Generations ago the bells were first fixed with an heir's hours. The eclipse over the altar has not moved since.
Seven seals on one uncut cord. They keep the kingdom running, and the throne empty.
A children's story about a court where no one ages. Most people think it is only a story.

production.direction_en: The square is set with long tables. Every guest must bring one dish and one name.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: Rule of the Harvest Supper: one dish, one name. You say the name, you get a bowl.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: I brought a dish. It is technically soup.

commands.speaker: jori_flint
commands.text: It is moving.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: It is effervescent.

commands.speaker: nixie_vale
commands.text: I will eat it! For the festival!

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: Nixie ate it. Nixie was fine. Nixie glowed faintly for an hour.

production.direction_en: The innkeeper explains why every traveler gets a free meal twice a day.

commands.speaker: oakhaven_innkeeper
commands.text: After Crownfall, travelers stopped paying. So we stopped charging. Twice a day, a meal, no coin.

commands.speaker: fadyme
commands.text: That is generous.

commands.speaker: oakhaven_innkeeper
commands.text: It is practical. A fed traveler says their name at the door. A hungry one slips past the register.

commands.speaker: mahmut
commands.text: So the meal is a count.

commands.speaker: oakhaven_innkeeper
commands.text: The meal is a meal, knight. The count is a bonus.

production.direction_en: Late night. Pippa leads the square in a song of every name collected.

commands.speaker: pippa_bell
commands.text: Last verse! Everyone who brought a name, sing it with me!

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: Two hundred voices, off-key and loud. Somewhere, a bell rang, and nobody stopped singing.

commands.speaker: fadyme_thought
commands.text: The bell cannot count a square this loud. For one night, it is losing.

production.direction_en: On their own safe route to the altar, Clem, Vespera and Thistle join highland villagers climbing to watch the far mountain where the eclipse hangs.

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Sun-Eclipse Day. Once a year the villages say the black sun breathes.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: Does it?

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Every grave-keeper's record says yes. Every scholar's says no. I trust grave-keepers.

production.direction_en: At noon the eclipse's rim flickers. Every bell pin, charm and bell in the valley hums at once.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: The owing-bells are all opening. All of them. The whole ridge.

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: It is not breathing. It is recounting. Every owed hour in the valley, checked at once.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: Why t-today?

commands.speaker: vespera_wisp
commands.text: Because someone set a day for it. Machines keep calendars. So do chancellors.

production.direction_en: The villagers give each traveler a stamped token so the eclipse will "know they watched".

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: Sun-Eclipse tokens. Superstition. I am keeping five.

commands.speaker: thistle_roe
commands.text: Why five?

commands.speaker: clem_marr
commands.text: One for each of us who watched. So somebody knows we were here.

production.direction_en: Kera nails the archive wing's first public notice to its own door.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: Salt-road fever in the coastal villages. The ledger wing sold the cure. We are giving it away.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: With what staff? You have three shelves and a temper.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: I have you, Iona, and a harbor archer who knows the coast.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: I did not agree to this.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: You agreed with your face.

production.direction_en: The salt villages. Tilda treats patients; Odelia guides them through her old harbor.

commands.speaker: tilda_fen
commands.text: This is where I learned. My teacher treated this fever with salt and honesty.

commands.speaker: odelia_pike
commands.text: My brother and I stole bread from that bakery.

commands.speaker: iona_mist
commands.text: Then we will pay it back with medicine.

production.direction_en: A ledger-wing agent arrives selling the same cure at ten times the price.

commands.speaker: red_vial_agent
commands.text: You are ruining a market, alchemist.

commands.speaker: kera_voss
commands.text: I am labeling it correctly. Yours says "cure". Mine says "cure, free, and the name of who made it".

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: The villagers took Kera's bottles. The agent left with a full crate and an empty road.

production.direction_en: A Council herald reads a new decree in the square Marek once spoke in.

commands.speaker: council_herald
commands.text: By the seven seals of the Council: any person claiming royal blood shall present themselves at the capital, or be recorded as an impostor.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: That is new ink. They know a claim is coming.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: They have never needed to deny a heir before.

production.direction_en: Sable lifts the decree from the herald's satchel while Nara blocks the view.

commands.speaker: sable_wren
commands.text: Seven seals. All uncut. The Council agrees on something for once.

commands.speaker: mirel_quill
commands.text: And this is a court hand I know. The same scribe who wrote the erasure orders I copied.

commands.speaker: nara_vell
commands.text: Then the hand that removed her name is still in the capital.

production.direction_en: Marek answers the Council herald in front of the square.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: You read what you are given. So did I. I stopped.

commands.speaker: council_herald
commands.text: You were a herald of the Crown. You know the penalty.

commands.speaker: marek_vane
commands.text: I know the price. It is cheaper than reading false paper for the rest of my life.

commands.speaker: narrator
commands.text: The herald left. The decree stayed nailed to the post, and beneath it someone scratched: WHO GAVE THE ORDER?
